links.caveat: On 64-bit builds lambda <= 64, so root_u = lambda/131072 = 0 and public inputs take the finite-size fallback. Nothing here exercises the recursive subexponential kernel. ic.tensor_contraction_v1 is an exponential toy (protocol H1).
links.isolation_reason: L0 ('recorded') is the level ecbench documents as sufficient for operation counts, which do not depend on contention; it is the lowest level the spec schema accepts. The EKS L2 gate refuses these panels because rho solves at 10-16 bits take under 1 ms (MIN_SOLVE_WALL_NS_V3 = 1,000,000 ns grades them L1; run gh-41008826427-1: 176/192 L1; exit 42). A counts-only session needs no wall isolation. Run with `ecbench run --cpus none` (L0 by construction) and a per-track --lock path if the tracks run concurrently.
links.order_note: spec orders are alternate_measured (C) and shuffle (B); the schema field above is the nearest enum and has no effect on counted S

question: On the registered bench-roster prime curves of 10, 12, 14 and 16 bits, what do ic.tensor_contraction_v1 (m = 2) and the four native hashed-base backends of ic.hashed_native_v1 cost in ecbench's counted unit S, how far is each from the matched rho.negation reference (distance remaining, per curve, across the AGENTS.md 5a pricing band), and how does median S scale with r? Counted S only; no wall time.

Track C, per curve: the paired ratio of summed S, tensor-m2 over rho-neg (the distance remaining to rho), with its paired bootstrap interval and the 5a band.

claims.if_not_supported: no ranking on that curve; the ratio is still reported as the distance remaining

Native S is a lower bound, so only 'costs more than rho' can be concluded; a ratio interval below 1 is reported as unranked.

claims.if_not_supported: incomplete or below-1: census and descriptive ratio only, no ranking

claims.text: Determinism: rho-neg and rho-neg-aa (both tracks) and native-selectors and native-selectors-aa (track B) share each (workload, round) algorithm seed, so their S must be identical row by row, and ecbench verify --replay-all must reproduce every row.
Wall time, speedups, asymptotic or subexponential behaviour, deployed-size curves, challenge scalars and full arithmetic pricing of the native arms are outside this protocol.

hypotheses.statement: The tensor arm costs far more than rho in S on every curve, and the gap grows with r (carried unchanged from crypto-ecdl-tensor-ic-speed-20261030).
hypotheses.mechanism: Each relation is found by exact contraction costing about |F_1||F_2| ~ 2r point additions, and N + 1 ~ 2(2r)^(1/2) relations are needed, so total GAE grows like r^(3/2) and S = GAE/sqrt(r) like r; rho's S is about 1 (total GAE like sqrt(r)).

predictions.minimum_effect: tensor-m2/rho-neg ratio interval above 1 on every curve, increasing from 10 to 16 bits

power.note: Family: C-rho, C-ic (4 curves each) + B-rho-{source,selectors,width,partial,ic} and B-source-selectors (4 curves each) = 32 per-curve tests. 8 paired targets per curve; the paired bootstrap resamples targets. One round: S is a deterministic function of (workload, algorithm seed) and exactly replayable, so repeating a round with the same seed adds nothing; further rounds would add new walk seeds per target (more power), which the expected H1 effect does not need and the 16-bit tensor cells (about 417 s each) make expensive. Warmup 0: warm-up rounds are unmeasured and only remove one-time wall costs, which counted S does not see; 0 is the minimum ecbench accepts (rounds must be >= 1). C-rho-ic and B-pos are reported but are not in the family.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Scaled from the 2026-10-30 session-log sizing (contended host): tensor solve 12 bits 3 s, 14 bits 21 s, 16 bits about 417 s; 10 bits assumed <= 1 s. Track C: tensor 8 x (1 + 3 + 21 + 417) s ~ 3540 s, of which the 16-bit cells are ~3340 s (0.93 h, under the 2.5 h split threshold, so 16 bits stays in spec-C); rho, rho-aa and ic-mitm 96 rows at ~1 s each; C total ~3.7e3 s (~1.0 h). Track B: 288 executions; worst case every native row (160) runs to its 30 s budget, 4800 s, plus 128 sub-second rows; B upper bound ~4.9e3 s (~1.4 h). Sequential worst case ~8.7e3 s (2.4 h); the two tracks may run concurrently on separate CPUs of the 4 vCPU host (counts are contention-independent), about 1.4 h wall. Within a spec ecbench executes curves in order 10, 12, 14, 16, so the smaller sizes finish first.

primary.name: S
primary.definition: every phase charged in ecbench.gae divided by sqrt(r); a lower bound for the native arms, whose arithmetic is not completely priced

secondary.name: unpriced native work
secondary.definition: every *_uncharged counter on every arm, rho included, priced at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per operation for the 5a band (ecbench band --weights 0,0.1,1; ecbench compare --weight w)

secondary.name: outcome census
secondary.definition: count of verified / wrong_answer / timeout / exhausted / error rows per arm and curve, with the exclusive phase where incomplete native attempts stopped

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: C 4 arms x 32 workloads x 1 round = 128 executions; B 9 arms x 32 workloads x 1 round = 288 executions; no warm-up; then stop
per-execution budgets are the specs' (C 1800 s, B 30 s and every native call's 5M-step bound); a row that hits them is retained as unknown/exhausted, never rerun with a larger budget
a row whose answer does not verify stops nothing and is recorded as wrong_answer

invalidation_rules: a row with outcome.status other than verified is excluded from ratios and slopes and reported in the census
a track whose ecbench verify --replay-all is not OK with every replay identical yields no result
a determinism control (C-aa, B-aa-rho, B-aa-selectors) with any row whose S differs from its partner invalidates that track's counted results
B is invalid if B.rho-neg-v2 fails to verify any target
any wall-time number from these sessions is descriptive host timing and is never reported as a result

decision_rule.text: Per curve, the gap of arm X to rho is R = sum S(X) / sum S(rho-neg) over the 8 paired targets, reported as the distance remaining (R and log2 R) with a 95% paired bootstrap interval (ecbench compare, 4000 resamples, seed 20261002), at weights 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per unpriced operation on every arm, rho included. X is ranked above (more expensive than) or below rho on a curve only when the Holm-adjusted interval excludes 1 on the same side at all three weights (ecbench band --ranks); otherwise no ranking. For native arms (lower-bound S) only R > 1 can be ranked. Ratios need all 8 rows of both arms verified on that curve; otherwise the census and a descriptive completed-row ratio flagged incomplete. C3 below 1 across the band would count as a measured improvement over the IC baseline; it is not expected. Slopes are OLS of log2 median S on log2 r over complete sizes, intervals by resampling targets within size.
decision_rule.threshold: Holm-adjusted paired-bootstrap ratio interval excludes 1 on the same side at weights 0, 0.1 and 1
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of summed S over paired targets per curve, candidate over reference (ecbench compare)
decision_rule.interval: paired bootstrap over the 8 targets per curve, 95%
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed S per curve (distance remaining to rho), and log-log slope
